deep.reconstruction:
This page is one sheet of a hand-computed table of squares of four-digit numbers N = 1000k + r, where k = 1..9 and r = 050..099 on this page. The previous page has r = 000..049; the next page continues with r = 100..149, there headed 11, 21, ..., 91.

How to read the table:
- The column headers '10, 2, 3, ..., 9' mean the leading digit k. The first header reads '10' because on later sheets the header carries the hundreds digit too (11, 21, ...).
- The row label is the last three digits r.
- Body entry in column k, row r = floor(N^2/1000) = 1000k^2 + 2kr + floor(r^2/1000).
- Rightmost column = N^2 mod 1000 = r^2 mod 1000. This is the same for every k because (1000k + r)^2 = 10^6 k^2 + 2000kr + r^2.
- So the full square N^2 is the body entry followed by the three digits in the right-hand column. Example: 5059^2 = 25593|481.

Abbreviation: only the last two digits are written, except where the higher digits change or at the head of a block.

Construction (my inference from the structure): each column is an arithmetic progression with difference 2k per row. An extra +1 is carried whenever floor(r^2/1000) increases. On this page that happens at r = 055, 064, 071, 078, 084, 090 and 095, where r^2 passes 3000, 4000, ..., 9000.

Spot checks, all correct:
- 1050^2 = 1102500
- 9050^2 = 81902500
- 4064^2 = 16516096
- 7071^2 = 49999041
- 8087^2 = 65399569
- 9094^2 = 82700836
- 7099^2 = 50395801

Purpose: a working table of exact squares. Typical uses are multiplication by quarter-squares, ab = ((a+b)^2 - (a-b)^2)/4, and sums of squares in least-squares and geodetic reductions. The page contains no derivation, only tabulation.

Several cells show visible overwritten corrections: row 064 col 2 (60); rows 065-069 col 2; 082/083 col 3 (9498, 9504); 061 col 4 (91); 057-059 col 6; 095-097 col 7 (39, 53, 67); 088/089 col 9; 068 and 087-089 in the last column; 093-094 col 9. results.what: Table of exact squares of 4-digit numbers 1000k + r (here r = 50..99, k = 1..9). It is split into a thousands part and a common last-three-digit column r^2 mod 1000, and built by constant differences 2k with carries from r^2.
results.modern_name: Table of squares (usable for quarter-squares multiplication)
results.usually_credited_to: Tables of squares long predate Gauss, e.g. J. J. Ludolf, Tetragonometria tabularia (1690). Quarter-square tables are associated with Voisin (1817) and others.

deep.surprise_reason: Purely routine numerical tabulation of squares by finite differences, a standard computing aid of the period; nothing mathematically novel.

checkable.asserts: Structure of the body entries: floor(N^2/1000) = 1000k^2 + 2kr + floor(r^2/1000).

checkable.sympy: all((1000*k+r)**2 % 1000 == r**2 % 1000 for k in range(1,10) for r in range(50,100))
checkable.asserts: The right-hand column r^2 mod 1000 is valid for every column k.

transcription_corrections: Header '10, 2, 3, ...' denotes the leading digit k of N = 1000k + r, i.e. 10xx, 20xx, ..., 90xx. It is not a multiplier.
Top marginalia 'Math 5' and '40c/5' are shelf/folio marks, not table content.
Row 099, col 8 reads 65693 but the correct value is 65593; this is the manuscript's own slip, not a transcription error, as far as the image shows.
